Blank completion, contrast clue (including received view then finding)
Blank completion, phrase options (word + preposition, a/an + word)

items.passage: Christopher Achen and Larry Bartels interpreted Woodrow Wilson’s diminished 1916 vote share in New Jersey beach counties after a series of shark attacks as evidence that voters punish incumbents for misfortunes beyond their control. Analyzing presidential elections from 1872 to 2012, however, Anthony Fowler and Andrew B. Hall found no systematic electoral effect of shark attacks, suggesting that the 1916 result is ______ voters’ general behavior.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Unrepresentative of means not typical of. Analyzing presidential elections “from 1872 to 2012,” Fowler and Hall “found no systematic electoral effect of shark attacks.” If shark attacks do not generally sway elections, then the drop in 1916 that Achen and Bartels cited does not reflect the usual pattern; it is unrepresentative of voters’ general behavior.

A.recipe: reversal: the challenged view’s reading of the result (ANT)
A.why_wrong: Indicative of means serving as a sign of. That is how Achen and Bartels treated the 1916 result, “as evidence that voters punish incumbents for misfortunes beyond their control.” The finding of “no systematic electoral effect” across more than a century of elections points the other way.

C.recipe: near miss: right direction, too strong (CONNOT)
C.why_wrong: Antithetical to means directly opposed to. Finding “no systematic electoral effect” shows that the 1916 drop is not typical, not that voters generally do the opposite, such as rewarding leaders after shark attacks.

D.why_wrong: Ancillary to means supplementary or subordinate to. The text compares the 1916 result with the general pattern in elections; it does not present the result as a secondary part of voters’ behavior.

sources.what: Fowler and Hall 2018, Journal of Politics 80(4), abstract: data on every fatal shark attack in US history and county returns from every presidential election 1872 to 2012 show no systematic evidence that shark attacks affect elections; Achen and Bartels’s New Jersey 1916 finding weakens under alternative specifications

items.notes: Subject: social science (political science). Key letter B. Band-7 moves: the only clue is a consequence the student must turn into a judgment (no effect across 140 years, so the one case is atypical: two steps); the reversal is the challenged view’s own reading of the case (indicative of); near miss antithetical to fails only on degree. Earlier WiC items key an artifact of on similar reassessments (w2b1_02, w3b3_01), so this one keys the result’s typicality instead. Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): indicative of 20,438; unrepresentative of absent; antithetical to absent; ancillary to 69,564. Key is the longest option.

items.passage: Store-brand and national-brand headache remedies are physically interchangeable products, yet Bart Bronnenberg and colleagues found that while the average shopper chooses the national brand 26 percent of the time, pharmacists do so only 9 percent of the time. The researchers concluded that the extra price such brands command for health products is, to a sizable degree, ______ shoppers’ misinformation.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: A function of something is a quantity that depends on it. The remedies “are physically interchangeable products,” yet pharmacists, who know this, choose the national brand “only 9 percent of the time,” compared with “26 percent” for the average shopper. Since the better informed pay the extra price less often, the size of that price depends on how misinformed shoppers are: it is a function of their misinformation.

A.why_wrong: A casualty of something is harmed or destroyed by it. The text suggests the opposite: misinformation sustains the extra price, since the best-informed shoppers, pharmacists, are the ones who rarely pay it.

B.recipe: near miss: right relation, reversed order (CONNOT)
B.why_wrong: A precursor to something comes before it and leads to it. That would make the extra price a cause of shoppers’ misinformation, but the comparison with pharmacists suggests that misinformation is what produces the extra price.

C.why_wrong: A palliative for something eases its effects. Nothing in the text suggests that paying more for a national brand relieves shoppers’ misinformation; the shoppers who pay it are simply less informed.

sources.what: Bronnenberg, Dube, Gentzkow, Shapiro, Do Pharmacists Buy Bayer? (NBER w20295; QJE 2015), abstract: physically homogeneous categories; pharmacists choose national-brand headache remedies only 9 percent of the time against 26 percent for the average consumer; misinformation explains a sizable share of the brand premium for health products

items.notes: Subject: social science (economics). Key letter D. Band-7 moves: a familiar word in a transferred, mathematical sense (a function of); three steps (the products are the same, the informed rarely pay extra, so the premium tracks misinformation); near miss a precursor to fails only on direction. attributable to is already a WiC key (w2b2_02), so not used. Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): a casualty of 46,751; a precursor to 38,574; a palliative for 39,851; a function of 8,622. Key not the longest option.

items.passage: Superionic water ice, whose structure physicist Marius Millot and colleagues confirmed in 2019 using laser-driven shock compression and X-ray diffraction, is a ______ substance: its oxygen atoms remain fixed in a crystalline lattice, as in any solid, while its hydrogen ions diffuse through that lattice as readily as they would through a liquid.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Paradoxical means seeming to combine features that contradict each other. The text explains that superionic ice’s “oxygen atoms remain fixed in a crystalline lattice, as in any solid, while its hydrogen ions diffuse through that lattice as readily as they would through a liquid.” A substance that behaves like a solid and a liquid at once is paradoxical.

B.recipe: near miss: fits the liquid half of the clue only (CONNOT)
B.why_wrong: Volatile means likely to evaporate or change suddenly. The hydrogen ions move freely, but the text says nothing about the ice evaporating or being unstable, and its oxygen atoms “remain fixed in a crystalline lattice.”

C.recipe: topic echo: a property of solids (ASSOC)
C.why_wrong: Brittle describes a solid that breaks easily. The text never discusses how the ice breaks; its point is that the substance is solid in one respect and liquid-like in another.

D.why_wrong: Inert means inactive or motionless. The text says the hydrogen ions “diffuse through that lattice,” so part of the substance is in constant motion.

sources.what: Millot et al. 2019, Nature 569: 251-255, abstract: superionic water ice has liquid-like protons diffusing through the solid lattice of oxygen; laser-driven shock waves and X-ray diffraction gave unambiguous evidence of its crystalline oxygen lattice

items.notes: Subject: natural science (physics). Key letter A. Steps: 2 (see the solid trait and the liquid trait, then name what their combination is). Band 6 by plan: a plain hard key with the clue after a colon, as in 3.4 (variable); volatile is true of the liquid-like half only. Protons simplified to hydrogen ions. Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): paradoxical 28,519; volatile 18,078; brittle 22,307; inert 12,899. Key is the longest option.

items.passage: Until recently, the deception involved in giving a patient a placebo was widely considered ______ to the treatment’s benefits. But Ted Kaptchuk and colleagues found that patients with irritable bowel syndrome who were openly told that their pills were placebos made of an inert substance reported significantly greater improvement than patients who received no treatment.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Intrinsic to means essential to, part of the very nature of. The word “But” signals that the finding challenges the earlier view. Patients “who were openly told that their pills were placebos” still “reported significantly greater improvement than patients who received no treatment,” so the benefits did not depend on deceiving them. The challenged view, then, is that deception is intrinsic to a placebo’s benefits.

A.recipe: near miss: right field, too weak (CONNOT)
A.why_wrong: Germane means relevant. The study compared an openly given placebo with no treatment, not with a deceptive placebo, so it does not show that deception is irrelevant; what it challenges is the idea that the benefits require deception.

B.recipe: reversal: the finding’s own conclusion offered as the old view (ANT)
B.why_wrong: Incidental means minor or not essential. That is what the finding suggests about deception, so if it had been the earlier view, “But” would introduce no challenge.

D.why_wrong: Deleterious means harmful. If deception had been thought to harm the benefits, a finding that patients improved without it would not contrast with that view, as “But” requires.

sources.what: Kaptchuk et al. 2010, PLoS ONE 5(12): e15591, abstract: it is widely believed that response to placebo requires concealment or deception; IBS patients given open-label placebo pills presented as pills made of an inert substance, like sugar pills, had significantly higher improvement scores than no-treatment controls

items.notes: Subject: social science (psychology and medicine). Key letter C. Band-7 moves: blank on the view being challenged (Until recently ... But), with the finding’s own trait (incidental) as the reversal; near miss germane fails only on degree, and rejecting it needs the unstated point that the trial had no deceptive arm; deleterious is ruled out only by the logic of the contrast. Steps: 3. Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): germane 57,248; incidental 19,860; intrinsic 22,064; deleterious 41,092. Key not the longest option.

items.passage:
The following text is from Willa Cather’s 1923 novel A Lost Lady. Niel, a boy in a small prairie town, has broken his arm and has been cared for at the home of Mrs. Forrester.

Dr. Dennison set Niel’s arm and took him home in his buggy. Home was not a pleasant place to go to; a frail egg-shell house, set off on the edge of the prairie where people of no <u>consequence</u> lived. Except for the fact that he was Judge Pommeroy’s nephew, Niel would have been one of the boys to whom Mrs. Forrester merely nodded brightly as she passed.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “consequence” most nearly mean?
items.explanation: As used in the text, “consequence” most nearly means status, or social standing. The narrator says, “Except for the fact that he was Judge Pommeroy’s nephew, Niel would have been one of the boys to whom Mrs. Forrester merely nodded brightly as she passed.” The people on the edge of the prairie are those who count for little socially: people of no status.

A.why_wrong: Consequence often means outcome or result, but people of no outcome would make no sense; the text is ranking people by social importance.

B.why_wrong: The “frail egg-shell house” suggests modest means, but consequence does not mean wealth. The next sentence ties how Mrs. Forrester treats Niel to his family connection, “Judge Pommeroy’s nephew,” not to money.

D.recipe: another sense of the target, near the key (SENSE)
D.why_wrong: A matter of grave consequence is a serious one, but gravity means seriousness. The text is not saying these people lack seriousness; it says they lack social standing.

sources.what: Project Gutenberg, Willa Cather, A Lost Lady (1923), Part I, chapter 2 (text copied exactly)

items.notes: Subject: literature (novel, 1923). Key letter C. Band-7 moves: a common target in its older social sense (people of no consequence), the way reserve is restraint in 6557f7fc, with a mid-frequency key (status) rather than the everyday synonym importance; two distractors are real senses of the target (outcome, gravity, the second close to the key), one is a scene word (wealth) that the next sentence rules out. Placed in the hard cell rather than the denser Wharton excerpt to keep each tier’s register near CB’s. Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): Outcome 7,470; Wealth 1,459; Status 12,280; Gravity 3,662. Key not the longest option.

items.passage: Bahamian artist Tavares Strachan’s practice is thoroughly ______: his projects have included undergoing cosmonaut training in Russia, launching a small satellite into space in collaboration with a museum’s technology laboratory, and transporting a 2.5-ton block of ice from the Alaskan Arctic to the Bahamas for display in a solar-powered freezer at his former elementary school.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Interdisciplinary means combining or crossing several fields of knowledge. Each example joins art to another field: his projects have included “undergoing cosmonaut training in Russia,” “launching a small satellite into space in collaboration with a museum’s technology laboratory,” and displaying a block of Arctic ice “in a solar-powered freezer.” A practice that keeps bringing together art, space science, and engineering is interdisciplinary.

B.why_wrong: Parochial means narrow or limited to local concerns. The examples reach from Russia to orbit to the Arctic, so the practice is anything but narrow.

C.why_wrong: Derivative means imitative of others’ work. Nothing in the text suggests that Strachan copies other artists; the examples are unusual projects of his own.

D.recipe: near miss: half fits the space projects (CONNOT)
D.why_wrong: Speculative means based on conjecture rather than fact. Space travel may sound speculative, but the examples are things Strachan actually did, such as “undergoing cosmonaut training” and “launching a small satellite.”

sources.what: Wikipedia, Tavares Strachan: practice examines the intersection of art, science and the environment; cosmonaut training at the Yuri Gagarin Training Center (Orthostatic Tolerance); ENOCH satellite launched 2018 with the LACMA Art + Technology Lab; 2.5-ton block of Alaskan Arctic ice shipped to the Bahamas and displayed in a solar-powered freezer (2006)

items.notes: Subject: humanities (visual art). Key letter A. Band 6 by plan (B4 hard): the abstract category the three examples share, as undifferentiated in 3.18; distractors are other categories the examples half fit (speculative for the space projects, parochial for a Bahamian focus). Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): interdisciplinary 32,400; parochial 22,657; derivative 31,569; speculative 12,208. Key is the longest option.

items.passage: Analyzing data from Massachusetts, economist Joshua Goodman found that school closures during heavy snowstorms did not measurably reduce achievement, whereas individual absences caused by moderate snowfall did. A closure, which affects an entire class simultaneously, is apparently less ______ than an absence, since teachers can more readily accommodate an interruption that every student experiences together.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Disruptive means interfering with normal progress. Goodman found that closures “did not measurably reduce achievement,” whereas absences did, and the text explains that “teachers can more readily accommodate an interruption that every student experiences together.” A closure, then, is less disruptive to learning than an absence.

A.recipe: near miss: describes length, not effect (CONNOT)
A.why_wrong: Prolonged means long-lasting. The text compares how much closures and absences hurt achievement, not how long they last.

B.why_wrong: Conspicuous means easily noticed. Nothing in the text concerns how noticeable closures are, and a closure for the whole school would hardly be less noticeable than one student’s absence.

C.why_wrong: Advantageous means helpful. Saying a closure is less advantageous than an absence would make absences the better outcome, the opposite of what Goodman found.

sources.what: Goodman 2014, Flaking Out: Student Absences and Snow Days as Disruptions of Instructional Time (NBER w20221), abstract: strong relationship between student absences and achievement but no impact of lost instructional time due to school closures, Massachusetts; teachers deal well with coordinated disruptions like snow days but poorly with absences that affect different students at different times

items.notes: Subject: social science (economics of education). Key letter D. Negation sits in a comparative (less ______ than), as in medium B5 items; the clue is the since clause plus the first sentence’s finding. Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): prolonged 5,313; conspicuous 6,466; advantageous 17,474; disruptive absent. Key not the longest option.

items.passage: Artist Kapwani Kiwanga’s ongoing project Flowers for Africa begins with archival photographs of the bouquets and garlands displayed at ceremonies commemorating African nations’ independence. Rather than copying an arrangement exactly, each florist Kiwanga collaborates with re-creates it in their own style, so the bouquets that viewers encounter are best understood as ______ the archival images.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Interpretations of something are versions that express someone’s own understanding of it. The text says that “Rather than copying an arrangement exactly, each florist Kiwanga collaborates with re-creates it in their own style.” Bouquets made this way are interpretations of the archival images.

A.why_wrong: Replicas are exact copies. The text says the florists re-create each arrangement “Rather than copying an arrangement exactly,” so the bouquets are not replicas.

C.why_wrong: A rebuttal argues against something. Nothing suggests that the bouquets dispute the photographs; they are based on them.

D.why_wrong: Precursors come before the thing they lead to. The bouquets are made from photographs taken long ago, so they come after the images, not before.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Kapwani Kiwanga: Flowers for Africa (2013 to ongoing) uses archival images of independence ceremonies; bouquets, garlands and centerpieces captured on film are shown to florists, who appropriate them in their own compositional language; the reconstructed arrangements are displayed and left to wilt

items.notes: Subject: humanities (visual art). Key letter B. Clue is a restatement in the same sentence (rather than copying ... in their own style); one near miss (replicas of), one order reversal, one unsupported. Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): replicas of 68,228; interpretations of 30,927; rebuttals of absent; precursors to 55,742. Key is the longest option.

items.passage: Antibiotic resistance in disease-causing bacteria is often regarded as a by-product of modern medicine. But Jesper Larsen and colleagues showed that methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus ______ the clinical use of antibiotics: one resistant lineage emerged in European hedgehogs, whose skin can host a fungus that produces penicillin-like antibiotics, before such drugs entered medicine.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Predates means came earlier than. The text explains that “one resistant lineage emerged in European hedgehogs ... before such drugs entered medicine.” Resistance that arose before doctors began using antibiotics predates the clinical use of antibiotics.

B.why_wrong: Nothing in the text suggests that resistance in these bacteria sped up the medical use of antibiotics; the text is concerned with when the resistance first appeared.

C.why_wrong: If resistance followed the clinical use of antibiotics, it would have appeared afterward, which is the view the text rejects: the lineage emerged “before such drugs entered medicine.”

D.recipe: near miss: a parallel, wrong timing (CONNOT)
D.why_wrong: Mirrors would mean that resistance rose and spread along with medical use of antibiotics. The text says instead that it emerged in hedgehogs before that use began, driven by a fungus on their skin.

sources.what: Larsen et al. 2022, Nature 602: 135-141, Emergence of methicillin resistance predates the clinical use of antibiotics, abstract: resistance in human pathogens thought to be modern and driven by clinical use; MRSA lineages appeared in European hedgehogs in the pre-antibiotic era; the hedgehog dermatophyte Trichophyton erinacei produces two beta-lactam antibiotics

items.notes: Subject: natural science (microbiology). Key letter A. Clue is a restatement after the colon; the received view in the first clause sets up the reversal follows. Beta-lactam simplified to penicillin-like. Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): predates absent; accelerates absent; follows 3,661; mirrors 11,715. Key not the longest option.

items.subtype: Blank completion: cause or consequence clue
items.passage: Deepwater rice is cultivated in low-lying regions of Asia where fields flood deeply during the rainy season. When the plants are submerged, two genes that researchers in Japan named SNORKEL1 and SNORKEL2 stimulate rapid elongation of their hollow stems, a response that ______ drowning by keeping part of each plant above the surface, where it can continue exchanging gases with the atmosphere.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Averts means prevents. The text says the stem growth works “by keeping part of each plant above the surface, where it can continue exchanging gases with the atmosphere.” A plant that can still exchange gases with the atmosphere does not drown, so the response averts drowning.

A.why_wrong: Hastens means speeds up. Keeping part of the plant “above the surface” would delay or prevent drowning, not bring it on sooner.

B.why_wrong: Conceals means hides. The stem growth does not hide drowning; it keeps the plant from drowning in the first place.

D.recipe: near miss: enduring rather than avoiding (CONNOT)
D.why_wrong: To tolerate drowning would be to survive while drowning. The text describes a response that keeps the plant from drowning at all, by raising part of it above the water.

sources.what: Hattori et al. 2009, Nature 460: 1026-1030, abstract: deepwater rice adapts to flooding by elongating hollow internodes that function as snorkels for gas exchange with the atmosphere, preventing drowning; SNORKEL1 and SNORKEL2 trigger the elongation; rice breeding in lowland areas flooded during the rainy season

items.notes: Subject: natural science (botany). Key letter C. Cause or consequence clue: the by clause states the means, from which the effect on drowning follows. All authors are at Japanese institutions (Nagoya and others), hence researchers in Japan. Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): hastens 28,457; conceals 30,131; averts 61,961; tolerates 42,475. Key not the longest option.

items.passage:
The following text is from Edith Wharton’s 1913 novel The Custom of the Country. In Paris, Undine Spragg is waiting for her old friend Indiana Rolliver to return a favor. Indiana’s husband, James Rolliver, is a politician.

She kept herself well in the foreground of Indiana’s life, and cultivated toward the rarely-visible Rolliver a manner in which impersonal admiration for the statesman was <u>tempered</u> with the politest indifference to the man. Indiana seemed to do justice to her efforts and to be reassured by the result; but still there came no hint of a reward.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “tempered” most nearly mean?
items.explanation: As used in the text, “tempered” most nearly means moderated. Undine’s manner toward Rolliver contains “impersonal admiration for the statesman,” but that admiration is balanced by “the politest indifference to the man,” so that Indiana is “reassured by the result.” The indifference keeps the admiration from going too far: it moderates it.

A.why_wrong: Tempering steel toughens it, but the indifference does not make Undine’s admiration stronger or harder; it keeps that admiration in check, which is why Indiana is “reassured by the result.”

B.recipe: near miss: fails on whether the admiration shows (CONNOT)
B.why_wrong: The admiration is not hidden: it is part of the “manner” Undine shows Rolliver, alongside the indifference. Tempered means that the admiration is kept within limits, not that it is concealed.

C.why_wrong: The text mentions “no hint of a reward,” but that is the favor Undine hopes Indiana will do her. Nothing in the sentence describes the admiration as rewarded, and tempered does not mean rewarded.

sources.what: Project Gutenberg, Edith Wharton, The Custom of the Country (1913), chapter XXIV (text copied exactly; the excerpt starts at a sentence boundary)

items.notes: Subject: literature (novel, 1913). Key letter D. Medium meaning item: a common verb in its non-first sense (tempered as moderated, not hardened); one distractor another sense (toughened), one a near miss on a single feature (disguised: the admiration is shown, not hidden), one a scene word (rewarded, from the next sentence). James Rolliver’s first name is from the novel (the James J. Rollivers). Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): Toughened 40,050; Disguised 7,583; Rewarded 6,664; Moderated 25,393. Key is the longest option.

items.passage: British painter Lynette Yiadom-Boakye is celebrated for portraits whose subjects are ______: instead of depicting real people who pose for her, she composes the men and women in her paintings from her imagination and from found imagery.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Fictional means invented rather than real. The text explains that “instead of depicting real people who pose for her, she composes the men and women in her paintings from her imagination and from found imagery.” The subjects of her portraits are therefore fictional.

A.why_wrong: Famous subjects would be real, well-known people, but the text says she does not paint “real people.”

C.why_wrong: The text says nothing about the age of the people in her portraits.

D.why_wrong: Nothing in the text suggests that her portraits or their subjects are incomplete; the text is about where the subjects come from.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Lynette Yiadom-Boakye: British painter best known for portraits of imaginary subjects, or ones derived from found objects; her work consists mostly of painted portraits of imaginary Black subjects

items.notes: Subject: humanities (painting). Key letter B. Restatement after the colon, as in 1.11. Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): famous 2,092; fictional 62,836; elderly 4,116; unfinished 9,123. Key not the longest option.

items.passage: Juana Azurduy, who led battalions of Indigenous fighters against Spanish forces during the struggle for independence in what is now Bolivia, was a widely ______ commander. Her leadership so impressed General Manuel Belgrano that he presented her with his own sword, and in 1816 she was formally granted the rank of lieutenant colonel.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Admired means regarded with respect and approval. The text says that Azurduy’s leadership “so impressed General Manuel Belgrano that he presented her with his own sword,” and that she “was formally granted the rank of lieutenant colonel.” These honors show that she was a widely admired commander.

A.why_wrong: Nothing in the text suggests that Azurduy was unwilling to lead; it describes her leading fighters and being honored for it.

B.why_wrong: The text describes Azurduy being praised and honored, not criticized: a general gave her his own sword.

C.why_wrong: The text gives no sign that Azurduy lacked experience; it presents her as an impressive leader who was promoted.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Juana Azurduy de Padilla: guerrilla leader in Upper Peru (now Bolivia); led the Loyal Battalions of Indigenous fighters; General Manuel Belgrano was so impressed with her leadership that he gave her his own sword; granted the title of lieutenant colonel on August 16, 1816

items.notes: Subject: history (South American independence). Key letter D. Restatement in the next sentence, as in 1.15 and 1.53. Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): reluctant 6,398; criticized 37,110; inexperienced 10,264; admired 2,811. Key not the longest option.

items.passage: Biologist Talia Moore and colleagues found that jerboas, small desert rodents that hop on two legs, move in a highly ______ manner when fleeing danger: their escape trajectories were considerably harder to predict than those of four-legged rodents sharing the same habitat, which probably helps jerboas evade predators.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Erratic means irregular and unpredictable. The text explains that the jerboas’ “escape trajectories were considerably harder to predict than those of four-legged rodents sharing the same habitat.” Movement that is hard to predict is erratic.

A.why_wrong: Sluggish means slow. The text is about how predictable the jerboas’ paths are, not how fast they move, and nothing suggests they are slow.

B.why_wrong: The text does not describe jerboas as careful or hesitant; it describes trajectories that were “considerably harder to predict.”

D.why_wrong: Uniform means the same throughout. Trajectories that were “considerably harder to predict” are the opposite of uniform.

sources.what: Moore, Cooper, Biewener, Vasudevan 2017, Nature Communications 8: 440, abstract: in field observations, bipedal jerboa escape trajectories are significantly less predictable than those of quadrupedal rodents, likely increasing predator evasion ability

items.notes: Subject: natural science (zoology). Key letter C. Restatement after the colon. Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): sluggish 11,947; cautious 5,680; erratic 16,787; uniform 4,122. Key not the longest option.

items.passage:
The following text is from E. M. Forster’s 1905 novel Where Angels Fear to Tread. Philip Herriton and his sister Harriet have traveled to Italy on a family errand, and Harriet has just burst into tears while complaining to Philip about Miss Abbott, a woman from their hometown.

Philip <u>governed</u> his temper. His sister was annoying, but quite reasonable in her indignation. Moreover, Miss Abbott had behaved even worse than she supposed.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “governed” most nearly mean?
items.explanation: As used in the text, “governed” most nearly means controlled. Although Harriet “was annoying,” Philip judges her “quite reasonable in her indignation,” so he keeps his own anger in check rather than losing his temper. He controls his temper.

B.why_wrong: To govern a country is to administer it, but a temper is not something that is administered; the text describes Philip holding back his anger.

C.why_wrong: Govern can mean influence or determine, as when a rule governs a choice, but the text is not about Philip affecting his temper; it is about him keeping it in check.

D.why_wrong: Displaying his temper would mean showing anger. Philip instead finds his sister “quite reasonable in her indignation,” which is why he holds his anger back.

sources.what: Project Gutenberg, E. M. Forster, Where Angels Fear to Tread (1905), chapter 8 (text copied exactly)

items.notes: Subject: literature (novel, 1905). Key letter A. Easy meaning item: a common verb in a concrete sense fixed by its object (governed his temper). Raw freq.txt ranks (rarest content word): Controlled 6,019; Administered 9,553; Influenced 7,234; Displayed 4,724. Key not the longest option.

items.passage:
The following text is adapted from Catharine Parr Traill’s 1836 book The Backwoods of Canada, a collection of letters she wrote after emigrating from England to Canada. Here she describes a hotel in Montreal.

The servants of the house are very civil, and the company that we meet at the ordinary [the shared dining table] very respectable, chiefly emigrants like ourselves, with some lively French men and women. The table is well supplied, and the charges for <u>board</u> and lodging one dollar per day each.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “board” most nearly mean?
items.explanation: As used in the text, “board” most nearly means meals. Traill notes, “The table is well supplied,” before giving “the charges for board and lodging.” Board here is the food the hotel serves, paid for along with the rooms: meals.

A.why_wrong: A board can be a plank of wood, but a hotel does not charge guests for planks; the charge goes with “lodging” and a well-supplied table.

C.why_wrong: To board a ship or coach is to get on it, but Traill is describing what the hotel charges its guests, not the cost of a journey.

D.why_wrong: A board can be a group that runs an organization, but guests do not pay for a council; the text links board to the hotel’s “well supplied” table.

sources.what: Project Gutenberg, Catharine Parr Traill, The Backwoods of Canada (1836), Letter IV, Montreal (text copied exactly; gloss in brackets and the footnote mark removed)

items.notes: Subject: literature (letters, 1836). Key letter B. All three distractors are other senses of the target, as in 1.19 (drew); a bracketed gloss explains the old word ordinary. items.passage:
The following text is from Sarah Orne Jewett’s 1896 novel The Country of the Pointed Firs. The narrator is spending the summer in a small seaside town in Maine, where she lodges with Mrs. Todd. Mrs. Todd has just introduced her to a visiting friend, Mrs. Fosdick, and suggested something they could talk about.

And Mrs. Todd, large and amiable, disappeared and left us.

Being <u>furnished</u> not only with a subject of conversation, but with a safe refuge in the kitchen in case of incompatibility, Mrs. Fosdick and I sat down, prepared to make the best of each other.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “furnished” most nearly mean?
items.explanation: As used in the text, “furnished” most nearly means provided. Mrs. Todd has given the two women “a subject of conversation” and “a safe refuge in the kitchen” if they do not get along. Having been provided with both, they sit down “prepared to make the best of each other.”

A.why_wrong: A furnished room is one decorated or fitted with furniture, but the women are not decorated with “a subject of conversation”; they have simply been given one.

B.why_wrong: Nothing in the text suggests that the women have done anything to earn a reward; Mrs. Todd has just given them a topic and a place to retreat to.

C.why_wrong: Burdened suggests a heavy load, but a topic and “a safe refuge” make the visit easier, which is why the women are “prepared to make the best of each other.”

sources.what: Project Gutenberg, Sarah Orne Jewett, The Country of the Pointed Firs (1896), chapter XII, A Strange Sail (text copied exactly)

items.passage:
The following text is from Willa Cather’s 1912 novel Alexander’s Bridge. Lucius Wilson, a visitor to Boston, has noticed a woman walking toward him on a quiet street.

She was a person of distinction he saw at once, and, moreover, very handsome. She was tall, <u>carried</u> her beautiful head proudly, and moved with ease and certainty. One immediately took for granted the costly privileges and fine spaces that must lie in the background from which such a figure could emerge with this rapid and elegant gait.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “carried” most nearly mean?
items.explanation: As used in the text, “carried” most nearly means held. The sentence describes the woman’s posture as she walks: she is tall, “carried her beautiful head proudly, and moved with ease and certainty.” To carry one’s head proudly is to hold it high.

A.why_wrong: To carry a load is to transport it, but the woman is not moving her head from one place to another; the text describes how she holds it as she walks.

B.why_wrong: A candidate who carries an election wins it, but nothing is won here; the sentence describes the woman’s bearing.

D.why_wrong: A store that carries a product keeps it in stock, a sense that does not fit a description of someone walking “with ease and certainty.”

items.passage: Young jumping spiders of the species Toxeus magnus are ______ their mother long after they hatch. Zhanqi Chen and colleagues observed that the mother secretes droplets of a nutritious, milklike fluid that the spiderlings consume, and that during their first weeks the offspring cannot survive without it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To be nourished by someone is to be fed and sustained by them. The text explains that “the mother secretes droplets of a nutritious, milklike fluid that the spiderlings consume,” and that the offspring “cannot survive without it.” The spiderlings are therefore nourished by their mother.

B.why_wrong: The text describes a mother who keeps feeding her young after they hatch, the opposite of abandoning them.

C.why_wrong: Nothing in the text suggests that the young spiders hide from their mother; they consume the fluid she produces.

D.why_wrong: The text never suggests that the spiderlings are confused with their mother; it is about how she feeds them.

items.passage: South Korean artist Kimsooja is known for her bottari, bundles of belongings wrapped in traditional Korean cloth. items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: A reminder of something calls it to mind. Kimsooja “typically chooses secondhand clothing and old bedcovers,” cloth that other people have already worn and slept under. Using such materials makes each bundle a reminder of their previous lives.

A.why_wrong: The bundles are made from the old materials; they do not take the place of those materials’ previous lives.

B.why_wrong: Nothing in the text suggests that Kimsooja objects to the previous lives of the cloth; she chooses used cloth on purpose.

D.why_wrong: The text does not claim the bundles are better than the clothes and bedcovers once were; the point of using old cloth is to keep its past in view, not to improve on it.

items.passage: Annapurna Devi, a master of the surbahar, a large stringed instrument, gave her last public performance in 1956 and asked that her later playing not be recorded. Yet her influence on Hindustani classical music was far from ______: she devoted herself to teaching, and many of her students, including flutist Hariprasad Chaurasia, became major performers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Minor means small or unimportant, and “far from” reverses it. Although Devi stopped performing in public, the text says that “she devoted herself to teaching, and many of her students, including flutist Hariprasad Chaurasia, became major performers.” Through her students her influence was great, so it was far from minor.

B.why_wrong: The text does not discuss whether Devi’s influence was formal or informal; it explains that her influence was large because her students became major performers.

C.recipe: negation flip: the natural positive word (ANT)

D.why_wrong: Nothing in the text concerns how quickly her influence appeared; the text is about how large it was.

items.passage: After 1965, Indonesia’s government presented Raden Adjeng Kartini, a Javanese noblewoman who died in 1904, as a dutiful wife and obedient daughter. Her letters, however, reveal a ______ thinker: writing to Dutch friends around 1900, she criticized arranged marriage and polygamy and argued that Javanese girls should be educated.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Bold means willing to take risks or challenge others. The word “however” sets Kartini’s letters against the government’s image of her as “a dutiful wife and obedient daughter.” In the letters she “criticized arranged marriage and polygamy” and argued for educating girls, so they reveal a bold thinker.

A.recipe: reversal: the trait of the official image (ANT)
A.why_wrong: Timid fits the image of a “dutiful wife and obedient daughter,” which “however” tells us the letters contradict; criticizing marriage customs is not timid.

C.why_wrong: Nothing in the text suggests that Kartini’s thinking was careless; she made specific arguments about marriage and education.

D.why_wrong: The text does not describe the mood of the letters; it describes what they argued.
